Note the type of bridge and the original design and construction records.
3. For each critical area with a structural defect problem, record detailed photo documentation with dates, locations (from multiples views), and measurements.
4. After collecting all the information, use a computer-generated comparison program that compares the original design records with the photo documentation of the current conditions.
5. Record accurate measurements using the following:
6. If time and effort allow, using a nondestructive testing (NDT) procedure, such as ultrasonic thickness testing, provides further detailed documentation for selected particular areas.
7. Use the accuracy of the computer-generated comparison program and the NDT information gathered to make the recommendations for repair and maintenance suggestions.<|endoftext|>
